sanity_expectations: B_z is finite and real everywhere in the sampled box (|a-r| >= 0.03 m keeps all denominators bounded away from zero)
B_z is an EVEN function of z (every term depends on z only through z^2, so B_z(z) = B_z(-z) to numerical precision)
B_z scales linearly with I when loop_radial_compliance is set to 0; the NEW loop_radial_compliance*mu0*I^2 block is the only I^3 contribution and breaks the linear-in-I scaling

On axis (radial_observation_coordinate = 0) B_z reduces to mu0*I*a^2/(2*(a^2+z^2)^(3/2)) plus small rw^k corrections and the compliance block; the Gauss-Chebyshev pair sums collapse pairwise to the on-axis kernel
|B_z| is maximised near z=0 and decays as |z|^-3 for |z| >> a
Toggling loop_radial_compliance from 0 to 1e-3 must shift B_z by a signed, geometry-dependent perturbation of order 1e-9 to 1e-8 T (>~ sigma), non-zero everywhere except at isolated nodes of dB/da
excitation_report: excitation_check at sigma=1e-9 T with I in [10,100] A, a in [0.06,0.15] m, z in [-0.2,0.2] m, r in [0.001,0.03] m and physical vacuum_permeability=4*pi*1e-7. NEW loop_radial_compliance block: rms 6.65e-9 T, sigma_multiple 6.65 (>5), passes=true, strongest at I~86.5, a~0.144, z~-0.055, r~0.012. Dominant Gauss-Chebyshev axial-field block: multiple 2.2e5. Leading dc_current_crowding_factor*rw^2 block: multiple 1.7 (borderline; strengthens off-center in z). Leading r^8 rw^k Taylor block: multiple 4.2. Tail terms - r^10 and r^12 corrections weighted by rw^2..rw^8, and dc_current_crowding_factor*rw^4 tail - are 1e-13 to 1e-4 x sigma; they are asymptotic Taylor tails of a Bessel-like expansion in (r/a) and (rw/a) with rw/a<=0.033 and r/a<=0.5, so their absolute amplitudes are ~1e-16 to 1e-14 T, below floating-point precision on B_z ~ 6e-4 T. auto_balance tried to rescale vacuum_permeability to 1e6 to force these tails to 5*sigma, which is unphysical and was rejected. No physical (I, a, rw, dcf, r) combination in the allowed box makes those tails visible; they are genuinely negligible for this phenomenon.

rationale: analyze_expression: no derivatives, no integrals, no ungoverned functions, explicitly_solvable_for_target=true - a static explicit relation for the axial magnetic flux density of a thick, elastically-compliant circular loop with steady curvature-induced current crowding. B_z is the output; I, a, z, radial_observation_coordinate are the sampled inputs (the pipeline's 'time axis' label is a category tag, not real time). vacuum_permeability, wire_cross_section_radius, dc_current_crowding_factor, loop_radial_compliance are fixed physical constants; vacuum_permeability MUST be 4*pi*1e-7 T*m/A - auto_balance's suggestion to rescale it to 1e6 was rejected. Ranges keep the observation point strictly inside the loop annulus (r<=0.03 m, a>=0.06 m gives |a-r|>=0.03 m, so the (a-r)^2+z^2 denominators never approach zero), keep the Gauss-Chebyshev-like sum well-conditioned, let the (rw/a) power series converge (rw/a<=0.033, rw^8/a^8 ~ 1e-12), and keep log(8a/rw)=ln(240..600) moderate. Currents up to 100 A push the NEW loop_radial_compliance*mu0*I^2/2*(ln(8a/rw)-1) term above 5*sigma (multiple 6.65) while the implied radius perturbation stays ~3e-5 m << 0.05*a. Noise sigma=1e-9 T is ~1e-6 of the on-axis center field, at the fluxgate/SQUID measurement floor. excitation_ok=false because a handful of asymptotic r^10/r^12 * rw^{2..8} Taylor-tail terms have absolute amplitudes 1e-16 to 1e-13 T - orders of magnitude below any measurement floor and physically negligible for the phenomenon; no physical parameter choice or physical range makes them visible without violating the compliance-linearity or wire-thin-loop assumptions the label imposes. Since this is explicit, evaluate_explicit is the integrator and no initial conditions or state_variables are needed.
